sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US solar and storage names benefit structurally from falling US interest rates, which lower project financing costs and boost residential demand elasticity, a durable tailwind through 2025.
Indonesian EV adoption is policy-led, with VKTR's bus electrification tied to government fleet mandates and local content rules, creating a concentrated but growing domestic demand driver.
Grid-scale renewables in Indonesia remain bottlenecked by PLN's monopoly and tariff negotiations, making regulatory reform—not technology cost—the key swing factor for sector re-rating.
sectors.ai: Buy selective US solar/energy storage names (SEDG, ENPH, RUN) on the post-rate-cut repricing and IRA-driven demand floor, but stay underweight Indonesian renewables until clarity on PLN offtake tariffs and project financing improves; use VKTR dips to accumulate EV exposure.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah stability and easing inflation are restoring real household purchasing power, a durable tailwind for mass-market FMCG volumes into 2025.
Formal retail channel consolidation and premiumization are shifting share to listed players with strong distribution, rewarding scale and brand investment.
Export-oriented consumer names (food, agri, fisheries) benefit from structural global demand and favorable FX, decoupling from domestic consumption cycles.
sectors.ai: Indonesian consumer/FMCG is in a selective re-rating, not a broad upcycle: leadership is concentrated in small/mid caps (EL, AGAR, BOGA) with idiosyncratic catalysts, while large caps lag. Position for quality names with proven earnings delivery and export/commodity-linked upside; avoid chasing momentum without volume confirmation. Trim into strength on names up >10% in one session, as retail-driven spikes fade fast.
